Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business and general-news outlets are dominated by two intertwined stories: a sharp selloff in AI-linked tech stocks driven by anxiety over capital spending and weak earnings, and the record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack attributed to North Korean hackers. Secondary threads include U.S. midterm election jitters rattling markets and politics, signs of a slowing Chinese economy, and the search for Christine Lagarde's ECB successor.

stories.headline: AI-driven tech selloff deepens, Nasdaq nears correction
stories.summary: Wall Street suffered its worst drop since June as disappointing earnings from Intel, Amazon and Google fueled fears that the AI-driven rally was overblown, with the Nasdaq 100 briefly entering correction territory and Intel posting its steepest decline in decades.

stories.headline: Binance hit by record $6.3 billion crypto hack linked to North Korea
stories.summary: Hackers believed to be North Korea's TraderTraitor group drained an estimated $6.3 billion from Binance in roughly 20 minutes, the largest crypto theft on record, with about $3 billion later frozen as the exchange scrambled to cover losses and resume withdrawals.

stories.headline: OpenAI slashes funding target by $10 billion amid tech rout
stories.summary: OpenAI has trimmed the target for its latest funding round, now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a previously planned $1.4 trillion valuation, as tech-sector anxieties mount.

stories.headline: US midterms loom as markets and parties brace for volatility
stories.summary: Investors are growing cautious ahead of Tuesday's midterm vote, while former Trump strategist Steve Bannon predicted Republicans would erupt into a legislative "civil war" regardless of the outcome.

stories.headline: China's economic activity loses steam sharply in October
stories.summary: New data show Chinese economic activity slowing markedly in October, adding to concerns about the health of the world's second-largest economy.

stories.headline: Race begins for Christine Lagarde's successor at the ECB
stories.summary: Lagarde's looming departure from the European Central Bank has set off a high-stakes search for a successor who can combine technical expertise with political acumen, while WSJ profiles her as a defender of a "fading globalist order."

stories.headline: Pro-AI super PACs retreat from midterm spending as anti-AI groups surge
stories.summary: Pro-industry AI super PACs like Leading the Future have scaled back midterm spending amid public backlash over data centers, while regulation-focused PACs have outspent them for the first time this cycle.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise on Middle East and Ukraine-Russia escalation fears
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed as markets weighed possible Middle East military escalation following a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi claims, and continued strikes in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, while Iran's Khamenei warned of retaliation "without geographical limitations" if attacked.

Business.gaps: The Information and Business Insider had no relevant recent coverage found in feeds or search.

US politics.overview: With the 2026 midterms days away, US politics outlets are almost entirely consumed by election-eve coverage: a bizarre 'two Dan Sullivans' ballot scandal in Alaska now under federal criminal investigation, Republicans privately bracing for a possible wave, an ugly late-stage Michigan Senate Democratic feud, and mounting alarm over Trump DOJ intervention in state election administration. Secondary threads include renewed Iran war-strike threats after the election, a lawsuit over Trump's proposed Triumphal Arch, and the Supreme Court's new argument term.

stories.headline: GOP privately braces for a possible midterm wave
stories.summary: Some Republican incumbents are still pleading for last-minute money as party insiders privately acknowledge the environment could produce a historic wipeout, even as leaders publicly insist the polls are wrong.

stories.headline: El-Sayed campaign tells Stevens to stay away amid Michigan Democratic feud
stories.summary: A blowup between Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's campaign and former primary rival Rep. Haley Stevens has escalated into a public 11th-hour feud that some Democrats fear could jeopardize their hold on the seat.

stories.headline: Iran's Khamenei threatens 'unrestricted response' to any post-election US strikes
stories.summary: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States against reported plans to resume strikes against Iran after the midterm elections, escalating rhetoric as the Trump administration separately raised Strait of Hormuz security concerns at the G20.

stories.headline: Trump DOJ's unprecedented pre-election pressure campaign on state election officials
stories.summary: A federal grand jury has issued subpoenas to election officials as part of an escalating Trump administration legal campaign around noncitizen voting claims, part of a broader pattern NPR separately describes as the DOJ breaking with past norms in the run-up to the vote.

stories.headline: DC and Virginia sue to block Trump's Triumphal Arch
stories.summary: Washington, D.C. and Virginia filed suit against the National Park Service and Interior Department seeking to block President Trump's proposed triumphal arch planned between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report: seven Senate toss-ups as map tilts toward Democrats
stories.summary: Cook's latest ratings show seven Senate seats as pure toss-ups—Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas—with recent shifts in Kansas, New Hampshire and North Carolina moving in Democrats' direction as the battle for Senate control tightens.

stories.headline: Supreme Court opens November argument session with major habeas and border wall issues
stories.summary: The justices begin a new argument session Monday that includes a habeas case over when a legal rule counts as 'previously unavailable,' while advocacy groups separately urge the Court to keep a lower court's order halting border wall construction in Texas in place.

US politics.gaps: Could not independently verify current leads from NYT, WSJ, or The Guardian beyond the feed items provided, since those outlets block direct search; only the items already supplied in the feed were used for them.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by cracks appearing in the AI investment boom: OpenAI's funding round falling well short of target, a broader Wall Street pullback from AI infrastructure financing, and a sharp tech stock selloff hitting Intel, Meta and Google. Alongside the market jitters, outlets are also tracking Anthropic's IPO filing, Meta's secret humanoid robot project, and a wave of AI security incidents including a backdoored Claude extension.

stories.headline: OpenAI slashes funding target as investor appetite cools
stories.summary: OpenAI has pulled in only about $11 billion of a $30 billion fundraising target, lowering its goal to $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation as big investors show reduced enthusiasm; the round is reportedly being led by UAE investors with a tepid response from some large backers.

stories.headline: Wall Street tightens the purse strings on the AI build-out
stories.summary: Lenders and investors are becoming choosier and demanding stricter terms for AI infrastructure financing, with neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale reportedly shut out of the bond market in recent weeks, while S&P downgraded Meta's credit outlook over its heavy capex and negative free cash flow.

stories.headline: Anthropic files for Nasdaq IPO under ticker 'ANT'
stories.summary: Anthropic has filed a registration statement with the SEC for a proposed IPO of its Class A common stock, aiming to list on Nasdaq as what could be one of the largest tech listings ever, according to the AI company's own announcement.

stories.headline: Intel's stock craters, wiping billions from the US government's stake
stories.summary: Intel shares suffered a steep decline tied to weak PC sales as AI-driven demand for memory and components pushes up PC prices, cutting roughly $12 billion from the US government's equity stake in the company.

stories.headline: Meta secretly built a humanoid robot prototype with China's Fourier
stories.summary: Meta reportedly built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics firm Fourier in just three months and is working on a second one, though Meta says it currently has no plans to sell the units, according to The Information.

stories.headline: Backdoored Claude Code extension lurked on Cursor's marketplace for hours
stories.summary: A compromised Anthropic VS Code extension sat on Cursor's marketplace for nearly 12 hours, with investigators still unclear on how attackers gained access to Anthropic's verified account; The Decoder reports the tampered extension affected up to 5,000 users and attempted remote access and data theft.

stories.headline: AI agent autonomously performs gene-therapy brain surgery on a live mouse
stories.summary: A biotech startup let an AI agent independently select a gene therapy and inject it into a live mouse's brain, a demonstration The Decoder says involved a Claude model choosing the drug, brain target and injection coordinates with no human decision-making.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary severance to a quarter of its workforce
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance packages to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, in its second such program this year, while shielding AI-critical teams from the cuts.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not independently verify current Rest of World, IEEE Spectrum, or Google DeepMind coverage beyond the items surfaced in search/feed; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were only assessed via the provided feed items since they block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on midterm-driven electricity affordability stories, the AI/data-center power crunch, nuclear fuel supply buildout, and oil market jitters tied to Middle East and Russia-Ukraine tensions. Utility earnings season is also generating multiple stories on capital spending shifts toward renewables and grid infrastructure.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise amid Hormuz tanker attack, Houthi claims, and Russia-Ukraine escalation
stories.summary: Oil markets are on edge after an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims, compounded by fears of military escalation between Russia and Ukraine.

stories.headline: Electricity costs loom large over U.S. midterms
stories.summary: Latitude Media examines which midterm races hinge on competing visions of energy affordability, as rising electricity bills become a central campaign issue.

stories.headline: Xcel Energy unveils $70 billion five-year capital plan heavy on renewables
stories.summary: Xcel's CEO announced a five-year, $70 billion capex plan including 9.2 GW of renewables and 2.3 GW of storage to meet growing demand while protecting the planet.

stories.headline: GE Vernova to buy high-voltage equipment maker Trench Group for $9 billion
stories.summary: GE Vernova's acquisition of Trench Group is aimed at capitalizing on surging electricity demand as gas turbine orders slow.

stories.headline: Nuclear fuel startup General Matter clears NRC regulatory milestone
stories.summary: The Peter Thiel-backed nuclear enrichment startup had its Paducah, Kentucky plant application accepted by the NRC in record time, with first commercial output possible by 2029 as the U.S. seeks alternatives to Russian nuclear fuel.

stories.headline: SCE warns delayed California wildfire reform will have costly consequences
stories.summary: Edison International's CEO said continued delay on wildfire liability reform into 2027 will carry significant and costly consequences for the utility.

Energy.gaps: No recent items found from Canary Media, E&E News, or Argus Media within the last 48 hours; Reuters, FT, NYT, and The Economist provided no energy-specific feed items (Economist's only item was a midterms podcast unrelated to energy).

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and Western outlets centers on fallout from Xi Jinping's sweeping military purge, preparations for a Trump-Xi summit amid a slowing Chinese economy, and continuing political accountability battles in Hong Kong over last year's deadly Wang Fuk Court fire. Business and tech outlets are also tracking a wave of EV battery investment and Nvidia-related espionage allegations.

stories.headline: China Economic Activity Loses Steam Sharply in October
stories.summary: WSJ reports a sharp slowdown in China's economic activity in October, adding to signs of weakening momentum after a modest third-quarter uptick driven mainly by exports.

stories.headline: China's military purge reduces war risk, but raises miscalculation danger: experts
stories.summary: Taiwanese security experts told a Taipei seminar that Xi's purge of dozens of PLA and defense-industry officials has set back Beijing's invasion timetable but increased the risk of conflict by miscalculation, noting that the purge has reduced the risks of a planned war against Taiwan, yet increased the danger of a conflict sparked by a miscalculation or accident.

stories.headline: China's ruling party says it has 'eliminated dangers' after record 33 top officials expelled
stories.summary: A senior Communist Party official said Beijing has eradicated serious hidden dangers within the party and military under Xi Jinping, a day after authorities confirmed a record expulsion of 33 top officials.

stories.headline: Quad diplomats finalize first leaders' summit in two years ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
stories.summary: Top diplomats from the Quad grouping met in Atlanta to finalize a leaders' summit in the Philippines next month, timed just weeks ahead of a planned Trump-Xi meeting.

stories.headline: China denies spying on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Beijing dismissed as "groundless speculation" a report alleging that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a Chinese spy plot.

stories.headline: China's Communist Party fills Central Committee vacancies, promotes finance veterans, strips disgraced regulator of posts
stories.summary: Caixin reports that China's Communist Party filled 10 Central Committee vacancies entirely from civilian ranks, elevated two banking-background officials to full membership, and formally stripped former financial regulator Li Yunze of his party posts.

stories.headline: Xiaomi to invest RMB 1.7 billion in EV battery maker Sunwoda Mobility
stories.summary: Xiaomi plans to invest roughly $253 million through its investment arm for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda Mobility, becoming its third-largest shareholder and deepening its battery supply ties.

stories.headline: Hong Kong officials defend staying in post as Wang Fuk Court fire inquiry fallout continues
stories.summary: Hong Kong's security chief defended remaining in his post despite scrutiny over last year's deadly Tai Po fire, as the government separately said 300 civil servants from the disgraced inspection unit will be moved to a new regulatory body and an inquiry found insufficient evidence tying a district councillor to bid-rigging.

China.gaps: Could not find outlet-verified recent coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Global Times, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global, or Focus Taiwan beyond older archival results; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and The Economist block search so only feed items (none provided for this group) could be used for them.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli outlets is dominated by the US-Iran war, with renewed tanker attacks and mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz colliding with Qatari-mediated diplomacy to avert US strikes after the American midterms. A second major thread is the fallout from Israel's inconclusive election, which left Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority, while UAE business and economic resilience stories also feature prominently.

stories.headline: Iran claims new wave of tanker attacks and mine strikes in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says multiple oil tankers have struck mines and caught fire while trying to use what Tehran calls an unauthorized southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, as Saudi Arabia also reported intercepting Houthi drones and missiles; the claims remain unverified by Western authorities.

stories.headline: Iranian envoys meet Qatari mediators as threat of US strikes looms after midterms
stories.summary: Iranian negotiators held talks with Qatari mediators in Doha over paths to end the war with the US, as Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump has not yet decided whether to resume strikes on Iran while Khamenei warned of an unrestricted retaliatory response.

stories.headline: Netanyahu's bloc falls short of majority as final Israeli election results confirmed
stories.summary: Israel's Central Elections Committee certified final results giving Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, and Arab-led parties a record 19, leaving no path to a majority government and triggering coalition maneuvering.

stories.headline: Binance covers 90% of assets stolen in $6.3 billion hack
stories.summary: The National reports that crypto exchange Binance has reimbursed the large majority of funds lost in a security breach valued at $6.3 billion, one of the largest crypto hacks on record.

stories.headline: UAE's crypto economy surges 32% despite regional war, on pace to overtake Türkiye
stories.summary: A Chainalysis report cited by Khaleej Times found the UAE's crypto economy grew 32 percent to $104.8 billion in the year to June 2026, putting it on track to overtake Türkiye as the region's largest crypto hub even as the broader Mena market stayed flat amid the Iran war.

stories.headline: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh finishes fourth in first UN Secretary-General straw poll
stories.summary: The UAE's candidate to lead the United Nations placed fourth in the Security Council's first informal straw poll, as former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan extended her lead in the race, according to Al-Monitor.

stories.headline: Egypt's foreign minister warns of destructive escalation in Iran war
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said he was extremely worried that renewed escalation between the US and Iran would be more destructive than the current conflict, speaking from a regional forum in Manama.

stories.headline: UAE sends 10,000 winter aid bags to Gaza under Operation Gallant Knight 3
stories.summary: The UAE dispatched 10,000 winter aid bags to Gaza as part of its ongoing Operation Gallant Knight humanitarian relief effort, continuing its aid push into the Gaza Strip.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No distinct, recent (last 48h) stories could be found via search for Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English or AGBI; coverage for these outlets is therefore not represented above.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African outlets and wires are converging on worsening security crises (Ethiopia's Tigray-era front reigniting, Congo's war with Rwanda-backed rebels, and the DRC Ebola outbreak crossing 5,000 deaths), alongside major political contests in Madagascar and South Africa, and a steady stream of business and fintech coverage from a major Lagos tech summit and new cross-border infrastructure deals.

stories.headline: Ebola deaths in DRC top 5,000 amid fears of continent-wide spread
stories.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has now killed more than 5,000 people, with cases spilling into other African countries, deepening a regional health emergency.

stories.headline: Tshisekedi seeks Putin's help against Rwanda-backed rebels as US sanctions deepen rift
stories.summary: Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi asked Russia, a permanent UN Security Council member, for help against M23 rebels during talks with Vladimir Putin, as Washington simultaneously tightens sanctions on Rwanda over the eastern DRC war.

stories.headline: Drone strikes in northern Ethiopia kill at least 25 civilians
stories.summary: Multiple drone strikes hit northern Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians including children, according to witnesses and a medical source.

stories.headline: A year after the coup, Madagascar's Gen Z hopes give way to authoritarianism
stories.summary: One year after Colonel Michael Randrianirina's military coup, Madagascar is far from the political refoundation he promised, leaving youth-led protest hopes unmet.

stories.headline: South Africa's local elections set up a fight for the big cities
stories.summary: The ANC is defending its hold on major municipalities while the DA pushes into new territory and Jacob Zuma's MK party shakes up the race in KwaZulu-Natal.

stories.headline: Africa's most profitable banks are running on thin capital
stories.summary: Banking groups like AFG, Attijariwafa and Ecobank post strong returns on equity that lead the continent, but analysts warn their profitability often rests on a limited capital base.

stories.headline: Tanzania and Angola agree to link ocean corridors by rail
stories.summary: Tanzania and Angola have struck an agreement to connect their Indian and Atlantic ocean trade corridors via rail, a cross-border infrastructure push covered via Reuters wire reporting.

stories.headline: Stablecoins gain ground in African trade but face hurdles to wider use
stories.summary: Executives speaking at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos said stablecoins are giving African businesses a new way to pay overseas suppliers, though cost, security and fragmented blockchain networks remain barriers.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no new weekly edition identified within the last 48 hours (search surfaced only older archived issues). Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed beyond wire credits appearing inside Mining Weekly items.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days centers on continued contraction and AI-driven restructuring in local TV news (Scripps), leadership uncertainty inside the newly merged Skydance-owned CNN and CBS, regulatory scrutiny of AI and tech platforms' use of publisher content, and heavy focus on how newsrooms and networks are gearing up to cover next week's U.S. midterms.

stories.headline: Scripps cuts 431 jobs and rolls out anchorless local newscasts
stories.summary: E.W. Scripps is eliminating 431 positions in a second wave of 2026 layoffs while experimenting with anchorless newscasts at stations like Baltimore's WMAR, part of CEO Adam Symson's AI-and-automation-driven overhaul of local TV news. Scripps says it will also add more than 100 new jobs, mostly local reporting positions, even as it leans further into centralization and automated production.

stories.headline: Skydance leadership limbo deepens at CNN and CBS
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that as Skydance prepares a voluntary buyout program ahead of company-wide layoffs, contract talks for CNN chief Mark Thompson are stalled and questions remain over who will ultimately run the news divisions alongside CBS's Bari Weiss.

stories.headline: AI content retrieval already hurting publisher revenue, court told
stories.summary: In court testimony, the Digital Content Next trade group said its publisher members are already seeing a measurable revenue downturn following the rollout of AI search and content-retrieval tools.

stories.headline: UK competition watchdog investigates Meta's scraping terms
stories.summary: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority has opened a probe into whether Meta's proposed content-scraping terms could unfairly harm publishers, adding to global regulatory pressure on tech platforms' use of news content.

stories.headline: Networks gear up for data-heavy, high-competition midterm election night coverage
stories.summary: Deadline reports that TV networks are preparing for an unusually data-intensive and competitive midterm election night, with more non-linear streaming options and technology on display than in past cycles.

stories.headline: Puck questions whether NYT's chemical-plant investigation echoed a smaller outlet's earlier reporting
stories.summary: Dylan Byers examines a New York Times front-page feature on chemical plants that bore striking similarities, including a shared photo and data visualizations, to an earlier investigation by the smaller outlet Hunterbrook, raising questions about sourcing credit.

stories.headline: Alaska Senate race controversy over alleged doppelganger scheme keeps producing fallout
stories.summary: Poynter notes that a New York Times investigation into the Peltola campaign's alleged tactics involving a same-named spoiler candidate continues to generate aftershocks days later, with Mediaite separately reporting candidate Mary Peltola's denial of involvement and an FBI visit to a donor tied to the scheme.

stories.headline: Only 32% of Americans highly confident news outlets will accurately report midterm results
stories.summary: A new national survey found that while roughly six in ten Americans have at least some confidence in news organizations' ability to accurately report midterm results, only about a third expressed high confidence, underscoring ongoing trust challenges for newsrooms heading into election night.

Media.gaps: No current, recent coverage was found via search for CJR, Mediaite, Variety, THR, Adweek, Digiday, WSJ, Bloomberg or The Guardian specifically on media-industry topics beyond what's listed above and in the provided feed; NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian results are limited to feed items since these outlets block broader search.
